newsitem.title: GREECE: Turkish warplane crashes in Aegean, pilot missing.
newsitem.headline: Turkish warplane crashes in Aegean, pilot missing.

text.p: A Turkish F-16 fighter plane crashed on Tuesday after being intercepted by Greek warplanes near the eastern Aegean island of Chios and one of its two pilots was missing, Greek Defence Ministry officials said.
Greek naval forces picked up one Turkish pilot and took him to a hospital on Chios, just off the Turkish coast. Helicopters were still searching for the second pilot several hours after the crash.
Officials said a pilot had radioed he was abandoning his plane after being intercepted by two Greek Mirage 2000s. No shots were fired during the interception.
Greece has initiated diplomatic procedures to hand him over to Turkish authorities, they added.
The incident occurred on the last day of joint Greek-Cypriot military exercises -- "Nikiforos" on Cyprus and "Toxotis" in the southern Aegean.
The exercises stem from a 1993 military pact between Greece and the internationally recognised Cypriot government, which controls the southern, Greek-populated two-thirds of the divided island.

Greece reported more than 50 airspace violations since Monday, when the exercises started. Greek fighter planes were scrambled more than 40 times to intercept Turkish planes on Monday alone, the officials said.
